question.text: A nucleus has mass number <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and volume <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>V</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math>. Another nucleus has mass number <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> and volume <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>V</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>. If relation between mass number is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>V</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>V</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mfrac><mo>=</mo></math> _______.

solution.text:
For a nucleus we can write volume: V=43πR3

Now, R=R0A13

Therefore, V=43πR03A

⇒V2V1=A2A1=4
